# Expected values for the removal of a building site (docs/rules/removal.md, "Taking a building site down"), captured from the original
# program in the emulator (ADR 0008): tools/GhidraDump/emulate.py, the verb remove (no phase routine, so the castle hands out nothing and
# the site waits for its materials), with the click b@x,y,T placing the site of the type T at the pass 40 and the click N=f@x,y, the remove
# click 0x4615cf, before the pass N. The lines are the verb's, cut to what the scenario watches: the click lines, the map bytes (m), the
# generator (rng), the counts of the tables (c), the settler of the worker (s14 is the castle's builder, s13 its digger), the site's item
# (b2) and the site's flag item (f2 or f3), each where it changed. The building and flag slots are one higher than the engine's (the
# dummies of the tables). The lines before the pass 40 are left out: the checks start at the first click.
# Not production code: no routine of the program is transcribed here, only values the program produced.

# The next two scenarios use the verb construct (remove with the phase routine 0x42965c at the last phase of each cycle), so the castle hands
# goods out to the site and byte 8 of the site's item holds a count: the low nibble the goods counted on the way, the high nibble the
# goods delivered on site. The lines are cut to what the engine reproduces: the site's bytes (b2, whose bytes 8 and 9 are the counts), the
# castle's builder (s14), the map bytes (m), the generator (rng), and the counts of the tables (c). The flag items, the other settlers, and
# the castle's stock are left out: the engine lays a hand-out on the castle's flag at once where the original's first settler carries it
# out about 130 passes later, so the goods on the flags and carriers differ by that stand-in, and the test empties the castle of planks and
# stones as ConstructionBuilderTests does. A line "pass=N fill2+=NN" adds to byte 8 of the site the growth of its counts that the engine
# does not model (+01 a good counted on the way, +0F a good delivered), taken from the b2 bytes of the emulator at the pass the original
# changed them. The window of the comparison is the counts' own: the click clears both nibbles, and the goods the stand-in puts on the
# flags decide nothing the lines list.
